newsitem.title: USA: Dole drops advertising in several key states.
newsitem.headline: Dole drops advertising in several key states.

text.p: By Alan Elsner, U.S. Political Correspondent
Republican Bob Dole, trailing President Bill Clinton in opinion polls by 12-15 points, will do no television advertising this week in several key states, political sources said on Thursday.
The sources, relying on television advertising tracking companies, said Dole bought no television time this week in most of New England except Connecticut.
In the Midwest, he spent no money in Illinois and Wisconsin and a scant $8,000 in Missouri. And in the Pacific Northwest, he bought no TV time in Oregon or Washington.
Dole is spending some $650,000 on national networks and $350,000 on cable stations this week, so he will retain nationwide presence on the air waves.
Clinton campaign officials said Dole's television buys appeared to indicate he was virtually abandoning the struggle in a number of states.
Dole also sharply cut his advertising buys in California to $327,000, out of a total of about $5 million he is spending on television spots this week.

Since advertising rates differ sharply from state to state, looking at dollar amounts may be misleading. For instance, $90,000 is a large buy in Arizona, where rates are relatively cheap, while $327,000 is a small buy in California, which has some of the most expensive markets in the country.
The sources said Dole appeared to be narrowing his electoral strategy aiming for a bare majority in the Electoral College, where 270 votes are needed to win the presidency.

Dole has also been forced to spend valuable funds to shore up his position in some traditionally Republican states where he currently trails Clinton. He is spending $95,000 in Arizona and $350,000 in Florida, both of which have voted Republican in the past several presidential elections and ought to be firmly in his column less than six weeks before Election Day.
The Republican nominee's main push appears to be in the following states: New Jersey, Pennsylvania, Ohio, Michigan, Connecticut, Georgia, Colorado, Iowa, Kentucky, Nevada, New Mexico and Tennessee.

A survey of state polls conducted by the Hotline political newsletter found Clinton leading in all of them. In total, Clinton led in 36 states carrying 416 electoral votes, and Dole led in 13 states with 87 votes.

Clinton's lead was 10 percentage points or more in 29 of those states with 341 electoral votes. Dole led by 10 points or more in his home state of Kansas plus Nebraska and Idaho, for a total of 12 electoral votes.
Dole faces an uphill struggle in many of the states he is targeting. For example, a Reuters poll this week found Clinton leading by 16 percentage points in Pennsylvania and 14 points in New Jersey.
The latest poll in Iowa had Clinton 23 points ahead; in Connecticut a poll this week put Clinton 26 points in front.
